description:
Surfaced by the bedrock-287 audit; scoped by the bedrock-gu0 epic.

`State.health` is consumed in exactly two places, both matching `:ok` literally: `do_wait_for_healthy/2` (impl.ex:236) and `notify_waiting_for_healthy/1` (impl.ex:309). It is never returned by any `handle_call` in foreman/server.ex, never logged, never emitted as telemetry.

So the three non-`:ok` verdicts — `:starting`, `:unknown`, `{:failed_to_start, :at_least_one_failed_to_start}` — are computed and discarded. The distinction between 'still booting' and 'a worker is wedged' exists in the code and reaches nobody. That is precisely why bedrock-287 (order-dependent fold) and bedrock-mxt (never recomputed at boot) both persisted unnoticed: nothing read the value closely enough for either to show.

## Decision

Log the transition. Not telemetry: the service layer has no telemetry/tracing modules, and adding the data plane's convention here for one value is more scaffolding than the problem warrants. Not deletion: the guides document recovery as using `wait_for_healthy/2`, and the verdict is meaningful once bedrock-mxt settles it.

## Fix

Log only on CHANGE, never on every recompute — health is recomputed on every worker health report, and an unconditional log would be noise that trains operators to ignore it. Level should reflect severity: a transition into `{:failed_to_start, _}` or `:unknown` is a warning; a return to `:ok` is worth an info line so recovery is visible too; `:starting` during boot is unremarkable.

Name what changed and why it is actionable — the failed worker ids, not just the verdict atom. A bare '`foreman unhealthy`' sends an operator hunting.

Depends on bedrock-n5h: that ticket routes every health change through one place, which is the natural single point to log from. Doing this first would mean adding the log to each call site separately and missing the next one.

## Test (write first, must fail)

- a recompute that does not change the verdict logs nothing
- a transition to `{:failed_to_start, _}` warns and names the failed worker ids
- a transition back to `:ok` logs at info
- capture_log around the real state transitions, not around a helper called in isolation
title: Foreman health is computed but never exposed, so no operator or supervisor can read it
